groups.title: Capsule (E28200ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 capsules at a time. Children aged 8 to 14 years: take 1 capsule at a time. Take the dose 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Do not give this medicine to children under 2 years of age; if it is essential, see a doctor first.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have ever had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to it; if the user is a child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are debilitated or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take this medicine continuously over a long period. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like) or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant (cough and phlegm medicines), another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). If you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids or other medicines, consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever and the like) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D48600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after illness; to relieve pigmentation (melasma, freckles) caused by sunlight, skin disease and the like; to help prevent bleeding gums and nosebleeds; to relieve angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and as a tonic.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 1 to 2 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have high blood calcium (too much calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a whole-body inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe kidney failure; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the child gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excess oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function or low blood protein; if you have gout; or if you are short of folic acid.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, an irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, cardiac arrest or reduced central nervous system function appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (201501ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute bacterial diarrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) at a time, 4 times a day. Do not take it for more than 3 days. Give fluids during treatment, and adjust how much fluid is given and how it is given according to how severe the diarrhoea is and the age and condition of the person.
groups.caution:
If diarrhoea or vomiting is severe and persistent, or if the person refuses to eat, intravenous fluid replacement should be considered.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child or adolescent under 18 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to it.

If diarrhoea continues after 2 days of treatment, consider oral or intravenous fluid replacement or consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

While you have diarrhoea, avoid raw vegetables, fruit, green vegetables, spicy food and frozen food and drinks, and eat cooked food (meat, rice) where possible.

If a hypersensitivity reaction such as skin rash, hives, angioedema or anaphylactic shock appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Lozenge (106306ATO)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the pain of acute pharyngitis.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and over: suck 1 lozenge at a time. Do not exceed a maximum of 6 lozenges a day, and do not use it for more than 3 days.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 12 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as fructose intolerance, galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, if the user is an older person, if you have severe kidney impairment, or if your ability to produce or clear mucus is chronically impaired.

Do not use this medicine together with centrally acting cough suppressants such as codeine or dextromethorphan. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before using it with antibiotics such as erythromycin, cefalexin, oxytetracycline, amoxicillin, cefuroxime or doxycycline.

If Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) appears; or — occasionally — mild upper gastrointestinal reactions including indigestion, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, and dryness of the throat and mouth; or — rarely — stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach or abdomen, stomach or abdominal pain, diarrhoea, constipation or loss of appetite; or — rarely — allergic reactions such as skin rash and severe acute anaphylactoid reactions (including anaphylactic shock), hives, urticarial erythema, angioedema, itching, facial swelling, difficulty breathing, a rise in body temperature with chills, or purulent rhinitis with a raised white blood cell count; or — occasionally — abnormal sensation of the tongue or a change in taste; or — rarely — numbness in the mouth or numbness of the arm appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (E92400ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for diarrhoea, diarrhoea with abdominal pain, an upset stomach, loose stools and vomiting with diarrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day after meals, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a newborn baby or a child aged 7 years or under; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms from a medicine; if you have diarrhoea with fever; if the user is an older person; if you have bloody stools or persistent mucous stools; if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had an allergic reaction to it; or if you have acute severe diarrhoea or diarrhoea with abdominal pain or abdominal bloating.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If there is no improvement in symptoms after several days of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Do not take it continuously for more than 3 days.

Do not take this medicine together with gastrointestinal analgesics or antispasmodics. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If allergic symptoms such as rash or itching, or — rarely — dry mouth appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E85900ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D, vitamin B1, vitamin B2 and vitamin B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during the growing years and in old age. Through the vitamins and other ingredients it contains, it is used to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain such as low back pain and stiff shoulders, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis. Through the vitamins and other ingredients it contains, it is also used for poor development of the bones and teeth, the prevention of rickets, beriberi and eye fatigue. It is used to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, once a day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have high blood calcium, sarcoidosis or kidney disease; or if you have kidney stones or severe kidney failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein; or if you have had kidney stones.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are short of folic acid. This medicine may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While taking this medicine, do not take phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, inflammation of the mouth, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, red spots, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive problems, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or fluid on the lungs appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E77300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 8 years and over: take 1 tablet once a day.
groups.caution:
An accidental overdose of an iron-containing preparation in a child aged 6 years or under can cause fatal poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which abnormal iron metabolism causes iron to be deposited in the liver and pancreas), haemosiderosis or anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are under a doctor's care; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; or if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids. Take care when it is given together with anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene, because this may cause high blood potassium. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If hives, itching, photosensitivity, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or coma appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin B1, vitamin B2, vitamin B6 and vitamin C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding and when strength is reduced during or after illness, and to relieve angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 8 years and over: take 1 to 3 tablets at a time, once a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria; or if you have gout or kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results.

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet once a day with breakfast, or as directed by a doctor. If you have morning sickness, it is recommended that you take it at midday or in the evening. To help prevent neural tube defects in the foetus, take this medicine from at least 1 month before you plan to become pregnant. If you have not become pregnant after 2 to 3 months, the dose may be halved, so that you take 1/2 tablet once a day or 1 tablet once every 2 days.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are taking another medicine that contains vitamin A or vitamin D; if you have vitamin A excess or vitamin D excess; if you have kidney impairment or impaired iron utilisation; if you have high blood calcium or high calcium in the urine; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Taking 10,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day during pregnancy may increase the risk of birth defects, so if you may be pregnant or are in the first trimester of pregnancy, do not let the daily dose of vitamin A exceed 10,000 IU.

The stools may turn black and the urine may turn yellow, but this has no clinical significance.

If you have to take tetracyclines, leave an interval of 2 hours between them and this medicine. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are taking antiepileptics or anticonvulsants (for example carbamazepine, phenytoin, primidone and barbiturates) or another medicine containing vitamin A or vitamin D. Eating liver, liver products, cheese, eggs and the like while taking this medicine may take you over the daily requirement for vitamin A.

Discoloration of the stools may occur, and uncommonly headache, nausea, constipation, stomach discomfort, indigestion, vomiting, diarrhoea or reversible discoloration of the teeth; rarely the urine may turn yellow or dark; and very rarely allergy, an anaphylactic reaction, hives and asthma, itching, rash, a local skin reaction or an excessive irritation reaction may occur.
